solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get round tip of iceberg? It can't, sadly

definitions.text: Get round tip of iceberg? It can't, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters are put into a new disordered arrangement
the tip of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of iceberg is taken

explanation.surface: A rueful remark about the doomed liner that could not steer clear of the iceberg.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IT CAN'T plus I, from 'tip of iceberg', are rearranged under 'sadly'; the whole clue doubles as the definition, recalling the liner that struck an iceberg in 1912.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous liner sank in 1912 after failing to steer clear of an iceberg, exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: Rubbish shot, finally, by England penalty taker

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word shot

parts.note: Chris Waddle famously missed a penalty for England in the 1990 World Cup semi-final shoot-out

explanation.surface: A complaint about a poor spot-kick by an England footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Waddle was an England footballer whose shoot-out penalty sailed over the bar against West Germany in 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or worthless talk is a synonym for rubbish in the sense of drivel.

clue.text: Character on television put into print

parts.note: a printed character or letter is a piece of type
a television is a TV set

explanation.surface: A TV personality's words get published.
explanation.definitionFit: To set text in type ready for printing is to put it into print, a printing-trade synonym.

clue.text: It's used for trapping snitch infiltrating ring? On the contrary

indicators.note: infiltrating signals one piece getting inside another
on the contrary reverses the stated roles, so the ring goes inside the snitch rather than the snitch inside the ring

parts.note: a nose is slang for a police informer, a snitch
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A question about a device for catching an informer who has penetrated a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, NOSE goes inside O, which fails; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles so O goes inside NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A running loop of rope or wire is a snare used for catching animals.

clue.text: Parcel pa distributed containing black fruit

indicators.note: containing puts one piece inside the rearranged letters
distributed means spread around, so the letters of parcel and pa are rearranged

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Dad hands out a package that has dark fruit inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' gives CRAAPPLE from the letters of the parcel and pa, and 'containing' wraps that round the black letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sour wild apple is a kind of fruit, often made into jelly.

clue.text: It measures current in the morning and energy used in new term

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

indicators.note: used in places one piece inside another
new signals that the letters of term are freshly arranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Describes a device reading electricity at breakfast-time and the power consumed over a school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns TERM into METR, and 'used in' puts E inside it to make METER.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument for measuring electric current in amperes, hence its name.

clue.text: Snake's angrier after losing its head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: madder means angrier

explanation.surface: Claims a reptile becomes more furious after being decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after losing its head' drops the M from MADDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A common venomous snake of Britain and Europe, also called a viper.

clue.text: Is stomach upset? One probably enjoys it

indicators.note: upset suggests something knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone has an upset tummy, then suggests they like it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the stomach complaint, but it rearranges IS STOMACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes pleasure in pain or suffering would probably enjoy an upset, the clue suggests.

clue.text: Roll along as turn right comes up, getting led astray

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means a letter shifts earlier in the word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so the letters of led are jumbled

explanation.surface: Driving instructions: rolling along, turning right, and being misled.
explanation.walkthrough: In TURN the R (right) 'comes up' to give TRUN; 'astray' makes DLE from LED.
explanation.definitionFit: To move slowly and heavily on wheels is to roll along.

clue.text: Particular esteem

definitions.meaning: a particular is a detail or ..., as in 'in every particular'
esteem means high regard or admiration

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a point of detail (in one regard) and admiration or deference.

clue.text: A politician and artist going round house for a jar

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An MP and a painter tour a home in search of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek two-handled jar for wine or oil.

clue.text: Talk about Olympic event with son

parts.note: the discus throw is an Olympic field event
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogy

explanation.surface: Chatting about the throwing event with one's boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate or talk over a subject is to talk about it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sir partied wildly, ignoring start of tooth decay

indicators.note: wildly signals a frenzied rearrangement of the remaining letters
ignoring means leaving a letter out
start of means the first letter of tooth

explanation.surface: A knight had a riotous party and neglected his dental decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring start of tooth' removes T from PARTIED, leaving PARIED; 'wildly' rearranges SIR PARIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect leading to dilapidation is decay in the sense of a building falling apart.

clue.text: Worry about Democratic party

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: care means worry or anxiety

explanation.surface: Anxiety over the US Democratic Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A small trained group or unit, often of a political party, is a cadre.

clue.text: Sing the praises of former lover set to come back

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lot is a set or batch, as at auction

explanation.surface: An old flame is about to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come back' turns LOT into TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise highly or laud someone is to sing their praises, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bolt's fast — thanks to him?

parts.note: the surface evokes sprinter Usain Bolt's speed, but read as a door bolt held fast, the person thanked is the tradesman who fits locks

explanation.surface: Suggests someone is behind the sprinter's speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Usain Bolt is the famous sprinter; 'fast' here means securely fixed, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: The tradesman who makes and fits locks is the reason a bolt holds fast.

clue.text: Ford, e.g., parking next to dwelling

parts.note: resident means dwelling, living in a place

explanation.surface: A Ford car parked beside a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' suggests the car maker but means Gerald Ford, US head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford was the 38th US head of state, an example of a holder of that office.

clue.text: Used to be thoughtful, dear?

parts.note: ex means former, what used to be
pensive means thoughtful

explanation.surface: Asks a loved one whether they were once reflective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear' looks like a term of endearment but means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of high-priced or costly.

clue.text: End of crowd by pitch — are bats extremely low-priced?

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of crowd
bats means crazy, so the letters of pitch and are are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cricket question: at the pitch by the crowd, are the bats cheap?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' suggests cricket bats but is slang for crazy, the anagram signal; 'End of' gives the closing letter of crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for very cheap, costing next to nothing.

clue.text: Cheat's fed up with a drug — almost strange

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: strange signals the letters are put in an odd order
almost means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A con artist is sick of a drug that is nearly weird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses FED to DEF; 'almost' leaves DRU, and 'strange' mixes A DRU into RAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle or trick someone out of money is to cheat them.

clue.text: Start of Chopin — it's in authentic concert

indicators.note: in places these letters inside another word

parts.note: real means authentic

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of Chopin

parts.note: it, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A Chopin opening in a genuine piano performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of' takes the composer's initial; 'in' puts it and the pronoun inside the word for authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo musical performance, often of piano works, is a kind of concert.

clue.text: Volunteers set out to get sample

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: out means awry, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: Volunteers start off to obtain a specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is Britain's Territorial Army, part-time volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To try a little of food is to sample it, so a small trial portion.

clue.text: Somebody let off alarm

parts.note: a somebody is a famous person, a star

indicators.note: off means wrong or not right, so the letters of let are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone set off a fire alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let off' reads as setting off the alarm, but 'off' rearranges LET to TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to alarm or frighten them suddenly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Raise cheer about beginnings of Enigmatic Variations

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: to elate is to cheer or make happy

indicators.note: beginnings of takes the first letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: Applause for Elgar's Enigma Variations.
explanation.walkthrough: The Enigma Variations is Elgar's orchestral work; 'beginnings of' takes its initials, which go inside the word for cheer, signalled by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something up or promote someone is to raise them.

clue.text: Concentrate on the house in front of me and you

parts.note: FOC stands for free of charge, which is what on the house means
us means me and you

explanation.surface: A suggestion to focus on the house ahead of yourselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the house' means free, abbreviated FOC (free of charge).
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate attention on something is to bring it into sharp attention, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Frank attacked applicant

parts.note: candid means frank
ate means attacked, as in ate into

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank assaulted a job seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but means candid.
explanation.definitionFit: A person applying for a job or seeking election is a contender for the post.

clue.text: Conservative list is fair

parts.note: to list is to lean or tilt, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A Tory roster is just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' is the nautical sense of leaning to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair as in fair play: sporting and honest, the sense of a clean fight.

clue.text: Clumsy, I knock over writer with front of trolley

indicators.note: knocking over means upending, so in a down clue the word is read upside down

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of trolley

explanation.surface: An awkward person admits upsetting a pen and a supermarket trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock over' reverses PEN to NEP; T is the front of trolley.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking skill or awkward in action means clumsy, a synonym.

clue.text: Sat around horse in this fashion?

definitions.text: Sat around horse in this fashion?

indicators.note: around suggests moving the letters about, so sat is rearranged

parts.note: to horse is to ride, mount a horse

explanation.surface: Describes how someone sits on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges the three letters of the first word; the whole clue then describes sitting with a leg on each side of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with one leg on either side of a horse is the posture described.

clue.text: At home, tire badly; beginning of afternoon's lethargy

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of tire are disordered
beginning of takes the first letter of afternoon's

explanation.surface: Feeling worn out at home, an afternoon slump begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TIRE to ERTI, then A from afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactivity or sluggishness, a tendency to do nothing, is lethargy.

clue.text: Working on DPhil — one's supposedly intelligent

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters of on and DPhil are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone studying for a doctorate is, supposedly, clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working on' seems to describe a student, but 'Working' rearranges ON DPHIL. A DPhil is an Oxford doctorate.
explanation.definitionFit: The marine mammal is famously reputed to be highly intelligent.

clue.text: Last text remembered? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words is used, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the final message is only partly recalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Last in the sense of furthest or outermost, the far end of something.
